body:
Problem:
`:restart` clears the argument list.

Solution:
Do not clear the argument list. Note that buffer list may change if
argument buffers are do not exist.

Closes #42002

comment_data.body:
This still affects the buffer list after the restart. Preserving the buffer list (instead of the argument list) is the reason for using `%argdelete`. The reproduction goes something like this:
- From the root of this repo: `nvim -- LICENSE.txt Makefile`.
- `:%bw` to wipeout all buffers.
- `:edit BUILD.md`.
- `:buffers!` to see that there is only a single buffer.
- `:restart`.
- `:buffers!` to see that the buffer list is different.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -183,9 +183,13 @@ function M.ex_session_restart(eap, extra)
   end
   vim.uv.fs_close(fd)
 
+  -- Restore startup file arguments
+  vim.cmd('%argdelete')
+  if #vim.v.argf > 0 then
+    vim.cmd('argadd ' .. table.concat(vim.tbl_map(vim.fn.fnameescape, vim.v.argf), ' '))

comment_data.body:
Unless we add a way to restore arguments without creating buffers (like with a new 'sessionoptions' flag suggested in the [comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42009#issuecomment-5749456881) above), I think we need to choose between preserving the buffer list or preserving the startup arguments.

Not sure which is more preferred.

comment_regular_data.body: if you `:argdelete` the first argument of an arglist "[foo] bar baz", that doesn't survive the restart because `argf` doesn't keep track; it will be the same when it should be "[bar] baz".

> if you `:argdelete` the first argument of an arglist "[foo] bar baz", that doesn't survive the restart because `argf` doesn't keep track

That is the inverse problem... I don't think we need to support that. `:restart` preserves (restores) the startup args. ~~If you don't want to preserve the startup args, then perhaps `:restart!` (bang) should drop all file args, maybe, idk... out of scope here.~~

Wait, actually it should be fine to just iterate the args list instead of `v:argf`, right?

But this seems like something the session should handle, it shouldn't be specific to `:restart`. Does 'sessionoptions' need a new flag that restores args?

This PR is fine as a stop-gap though.

> But this seems like something the session should handle, it shouldn't be specific to `:restart`. Does 'sessionoptions' need a new flag that restores args?

i'm guessing that this is a different issue from the one i opened then? this should resolve what i originally came here for.

>this should resolve what i originally came here for
>
This PR solves the issue of not wiping the arglist. Whether we restore startup args or restore args at the time or `:restart` seems to be a matter of preference.

> That is the inverse problem... I don't think we need to support that.

> This PR solves the issue of not wiping the arglist.

i disagree with this interpretation of the issue on the grounds that the "arglist" and the "startup arguments" are only tangentially related, as the latter seeds the former but the former can (and in my case does) diverge.

> Preserving the buffer list (instead of the argument list) is the reason for using `%argdelete`

Reading the doc for `:restart` with/without "!", I think this makes sense?:

- the current logic in this PR applies to the "!" case (i.e. `v:argf` decides the args)
- for the non-"!" case, ignore `v:argf` and let the args list be restored by session. I.e. just skip the `:%argdelete` logic?

> * for the non-"!" case, ignore `v:argf` and let the args list be restored by session. I.e. just skip the `:%argdelete` logic?

For me, the main idea behind `:restart` is to "restart, but keep as much in place as possible". The fact that it uses Vim sessions is the implementation detail, which is used as the closest/easiest proxy to the final task.

Skipping `:%argdelete` will alter buffer list, which to me is (much) more severe intrusion than removing argument list. The most proper way would be to indeed have session restore arglist without affecting the final buffer list. Like either with a dedicate 'sessionoptions' flag or by some custom logic of smart removing argument buffers (without affecting order of the final buffer list).

> The fact that it uses Vim sessions is the implementation detail, which is used as the closest/easiest proxy to the final task

It is an "implementation detail" whose bugs should be fixed in that implementation, not as a special-case of restart.

c7947d2ed323d12053a54f33333c2a1472be0954 now changes to preserve the argument list as it exists at the time of `:restart`.

But it seems that it was preferred to preserve buffers rather than preserve arguments. So closing this and opened #42033 instead.

> preferred to preserve buffers rather than preserve arguments

I think dropping the `%argdelete` would be a useful compromise. IIUC the repro given at https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42009#discussion_r4056868483 , the worst case is that the restart includes extra buffers. That seems fine?

The current situation is that args are never preserved. If we drop `%argdelete` then buffers *and* args are preserved. "`:%bw` to wipeout all buffers" did not delete args so there is no reason to expect that args are deleted on restart.

> > preferred to preserve buffers rather than preserve arguments
> 
> I think dropping the `%argdelete` would be a useful compromise. IIUC the repro given at [#42009 (comment)](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42009#discussion_r4056868483) , the worst case is that the restart includes extra buffers. That seems fine?
> 
> The current situation is that args are never preserved. If we drop `%argdelete` then buffers _and_ args are preserved. "`:%bw` to wipeout all buffers" did not delete args so there is no reason to expect that args are deleted on restart.

My interpretation of "preserve buffer list" is that it is preserved *exactly*. I.e. 1) all listed buffers are preserved, 2) in the order they are, 3) without adding new ones.

Dropping `%argdelete` drops both 2 and 3, which (in my experience and taste) becomes annoying quite fast. I agree that avoiding deleting arguments is better (ideally that `:mksession` output script itself restores arguments without affecting buffer list), but I'd much rather prefer the guarantee to keep the buffer list instead.

> (ideally that `:mksession` output script itself restores arguments without affecting buffer list), 

That would change how args work entirely?

> but I'd much rather prefer the guarantee to keep the buffer list instead.

Users can already do that by deleting the args.
